name: Matteo Falco
note: Named as the father in the baptisms of at least five children at Arienzo between 1767 and 1786, and again in his son Giuseppe's marriage record. He appears as a witness at an Arienzo marriage in 1759, so he was an adult by then. He replaces the Agostino Falcone previously carried at the head of this line. **A third child, found in 1822, names them again — and earliest of all.** On 17 October 1822 **ANGELA FALCO**, fifty-one, widow of Crescenzo Rivetti, died on strada Capodiuomo, «figlia di MATTEO FALCO Defunto, di professione Contadino, e di FRANCESCA CRISCI Defunta». Born about 1771. The founding couple is now named from the death acts of THREE separate children — Angela's in 1822, Rosa's in 1830 and Pasquale's in 1834 — and Angela's is the earliest. It also resolves an act found earlier in this research: when her husband Crescenzo Rivetti died in December 1816, **Gioacchino Falco** and **Giuseppe Falco** declared it as «parenti del defunto». They were his wife's brothers — which makes **Gioacchino Falco a strong candidate for a fifth child of Matteo and Francesca**, though no record yet names his parents.

name: Pasquale (Pascuale) Falco
note: Baptised in the Collegiate Church of Sant'Andrea at Arienzo on 24 October 1767 — the record names his father Matteo and his mother Francesca Crisci. He married Chiara Rivetti and their children were baptised in the same church from 1789 to 1802. He died at five in the morning on 1 October 1834 at his own house on strada Camellara; the civil act, given by two neighbours, names him husband of Chiara Rivetti and son of the late Matteo Falco and the late Francesca Crisci — confirming the 1767 baptism from an entirely separate record series. It gives his age as 74, which the baptism does not support; stated ages in these registers are approximate. **A daughter found in 1820 adds a third independent sighting.** On 23 August 1820 his daughter **ANNA FALCO**, twenty-five, wife of Arcangelo Crisci, died on strada Camellara, and her act names her «figlia di PASQUALE FALCO, di professione Contadino, domiciliato ivi strada Camellara, e di CHIARA RIVETTI, domiciliata ivi» — **both parents WITHOUT «fu»**. So Pasquale was alive, a contadino, and on the family's street in August 1820, fourteen years before his own death act; and Chiara, whom no record but her 1843 burial had ever named, was alive beside him. Anna was born about 1795 and had buried a two-day-old son seven months earlier. **And once, in 1824, he speaks for himself.** On 25 March 1824 the register opens: «sono comparsi **PASQUALE FALCO**, di anni **cinquantacinque**, di professione **COLONO**, regnicolo, domiciliato in questo comune, **strada Camellara**, vicino del defunto, e **GIUSEPPE FALCO**, di anni quarantadue, di professione colono, domiciliato ivi strada Camellara» — the two brothers together, reporting a neighbour's five-year-old dead. **It is the only record in which Pasquale acts rather than being named**: everywhere else somebody else is speaking of him. It gives his trade as *colono*, a tenant farmer, where his death act ten years later calls him *contadino*; and his age as fifty-five, one year out against the baptism of 1767, which is ordinary in these registers. **HER PARENTS ARE NOW NAMED BY A CIVIL ACT.** She died on 3 September 1843 at eight in the evening, in her own house, aged eighty, a *contadina*: «CHIARA RIVETTI VEDOVA DI PASQUALE FALCO … figlia di NICOLA RIVETTI defunto, di professione CONTADINO, e di ANNA DI RUGGIO defunta». The archive had carried two rival couples for her parents since 2026 — the gentry Don Nicola Rivetti and Donn'Anna Quotolo, and the labouring Nicola Rivetti and Anna di Ruggio — and had said the labouring couple was the better fit without claiming it. The act settles it: her father was a contadino.

name: Vincenzo Falco
note: His civil marriage act — Arienzo, act 26 of 15 December 1814 — records him as aged 21, a contadino, and “figlio maggiore di Pasquale Falco”: eldest son, and his father named without “fu”, so Pasquale was still living. His wife Andreana is “figlia di Arcangelo”. The parish record of the same marriage names his mother Chiara Rivetti and Andreana's mother Ruggiero. His death record of 15 May 1875 names Pasquale a third time. The civil death registers place his household on strada Camellara at Arienzo, the same street as his father’s, and name him with his wife Andreana Crisci. He called a son Pasquale after his father twice: the first died aged three on 22 February 1833, while the grandfather still lived; the second was born about a fortnight after the grandfather’s death and lived ten days, dying on Christmas Day 1834.

name: Raffaele Falco
note: Baptised at Arienzo in 1818 — “ex Vincentio Falco, e Andreana Crisci coniugibus huius Parochiae, cui imposuit nomen Raphael”, with Gelsumina Ruggiero as godmother. His death record of 21 April 1880 names his father as Vincenzo. His wife Angela Rosa Morgillo, daughter of Orazio, died six days before him. His civil birth act — Arienzo, act 47 of 10 May 1818 — has him born at three in the afternoon in his father's own house on strada Camellara, and gives both parents' ages: Vincenzo twenty-seven, Andreana Crisci twenty. It is the first record to date her at all, putting her birth about 1798 and her marriage, in December 1814, at about sixteen. **The complication is now closed.** Vincenzo and Andreana had named an earlier son Raffaele on 25 April 1816, and for a time this archive could not say which of the two was generation four — the generation was carried as *disputed*. The 1817 death register settles it: on **28 October 1817** the first Raffaele was buried, «figlio di Vincenzo Falco, e d'Andreana Crisci», aged about eighteen months. The child of 10 May 1818 is the one who lived. The burial was declared by **Giuseppe Falco, 37, massaro di campagna of strada Camellara**, called a «parente» of the family — a documented son of Matteo, and so Vincenzo's uncle. One warning survives: the two birth acts give irreconcilable ages for the father, Vincenzo thirty-five in 1816 and twenty-seven in 1818.

name: Carmine Antonio Falco
note: Birth record of 10 July 1850 names his father as Raffaele. Five further children recorded at Arienzo, 1873–1883.

name: Raffaele Falco
note: A farmer of Arienzo. His last recorded child, Gerardo, was born in 1913 not at Arienzo but at Arpaia, over the provincial border — the first sign of the move north.

name: Carmine Antonio (Carminantonio) Falco
note: Born at Arienzo, resident in the province of Benevento, died at Brisbane and buried at Nudgee Cemetery in niche CHAP-082-B2. His wife Filomena Annecchino died on 10 August 1988 and lies beside him in B1. Two of their sons, Carmine and Raffaele, married two Zampiello sisters of Arpaia and both brought their families to Brisbane.

name: Carmine Falco
note: Born at Forchia in the Valle Caudina. He and Francesca reached Brisbane on the ss «Sydney» of the Lauro Lines, out of Naples, arriving 26 MARCH 1964 — the Quarantine Service passenger list of that voyage enters them at numbers 492 and 493, bound for 43 Mount Joy, Petrie Terrace, Brisbane, an address given on 2 September 1963. Two further passengers of the same surname travel with them and are withheld here. The archive previously said «about 1957»; that was an inference from the 1957–1977 span of their Brisbane immigration file, and the passenger list corrects it. Francesca died at Brisbane on 10 September 2022 and is buried at Nudgee, plot V-0949.

name: Giuseppina Falco
note: Born at Benevento; her twin daughters were born at Brisbane in 1988.
